headline: Makes the Churchill museum in Fulton, Missouri, a National Historic Landmark and orders a study on adding it to the National Park System.
what_it_does: This law names America's National Churchill Museum, including the Winston Churchill Memorial at Westminster College in Fulton, Missouri, a National Historic Landmark. Churchill gave his famous 'Iron Curtain' speech at the college in 1946. The Department of the Interior may make agreements with public and private groups and give them technical and financial help to protect the site and offer education to visitors. Interior must also study whether the site should become part of the National Park System, look at other options, and estimate their costs.

who_it_affects.group: Westminster College and the Churchill museum
who_it_affects.how: The site gets landmark status and may receive federal technical and financial help through partnership agreements.

who_it_affects.group: Public and private groups that partner with the site
who_it_affects.how: They may enter cooperative agreements with the Interior Department and receive help to protect the site and run educational programs.
It must carry out a study on whether to add the site to the National Park System, including other options and cost estimates.
They may see added educational and interpretive facilities if partnership agreements are made.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted November 10, 2026; the summary gives no separate start date or study deadline.
